source.title: On the Power-Law Spectrum in Deep Learning: A Bridge to Protein Science
source.authors: Zeke Xie; Qian-Yuan Tang; Yunfeng Cai; Ming-Ming Sun; P. Li

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures Hessian spectrum properties and their association with test performance and generalization; this is a different measurement of properties named in V7, not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified there.
record.gate_note: Relevant results measure Hessian spectra and test error or state that trained networks generalize poorly; the paper does not test the claim versions' main interventions. Figure-only condition comparisons are not extracted as numeric rows. Cited prior work is not treated as this study's result.
record.test_reason: Figures 3 and 15 report LeNet test error across SGD and adaptive optimizers on MNIST and CIFAR-10, bearing on V4 in these settings. SGD learning rates are selected from a grid; adaptive methods use defaults. The extracted text does not preserve optimizer-specific point positions, so the direction of those comparisons cannot be established. Hessian spectral results do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report approximate power-law Hessian spectra in well-trained networks, propose spectral slope as an indicator of sharpness and test performance, and argue that trained networks lacking decaying spectra usually generalize poorly. Their maximum-entropy interpretation and proposed spectral parallel with proteins are also central conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies Hessian spectral structure and correlations, rather than testing the listed interventions or the magnitude-aware perturbation measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports spectral behavior varies with optimizer, batch size, model depth and width, training-set size, and label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral slope correlates with LeNet test error across optimizers: Pearson correlations are 0.853 on MNIST and 0.72 on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The fitted Hessian spectral slope predicts test error across these optimizer settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral slope correlates with the largest Hessian eigenvalue and Hessian trace on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian spectral slope tracks unnormalized curvature measures in the tested LeNet settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The reported tests reject power-law spectral fits for randomly initialized LeNet and do not reject them for the listed trained networks and eigengaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The upper Hessian spectrum and eigengaps often exhibit approximate power laws after training, depending on model and training conditions.

record.problems: The reported correlation values are figures without uncertainty estimates; optimizer-specific accuracy values are not given in the supplied text. Hessian-spectrum fit is not itself a direct measure of generalization gap.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only numeric comparisons for label noise, training-set size, batch size, model depth/width, and ResNet18 were not extracted as rows because they do not directly measure a named version's outcome or provide exact values in text. Cited results from prior studies were excluded.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and random-label training accuracy and held-out accuracy. Random-label experiments report spectra only.
Test error beyond the width needed for zero training error; width experiments report spectra.
Convolutional-versus-fully-connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and matched training-performance comparisons.
Held-out performance across batch sizes and recipe adaptations. Fixed-epoch spectral comparisons and interpretations about generalization do not supply that outcome.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Weight-magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with train-test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining to measure test accuracy.

missing.what: Optimizer-specific LeNet test errors and SGD baselines from the plotted comparisons. These directly bear on V4, but the supplied text retains only axis ranges, legends, and aggregate correlations; optimizer rankings cannot be recovered reliably. No verdict is assigned without readable comparisons.
missing.locator: Section 4, Figure 3; Appendix E, Figure 15; optimizer settings in Appendix B.2–B.3

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numbers match the supplied text. None of the existing rows directly measures a claim-version outcome. Non-rejection of a power-law fit should not be described as proof that the distribution is power-law. The source also contains inconsistent prose about the KS rejection inequality; its tables classify distances below the critical value as non-rejections.

versions.untested_parts: Whether the same architectures and recipes fit random labels and generalize on natural labels; no corresponding accuracy comparison is reported.
Test error across width beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under the stated tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch test performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.

It measures Hessian slope magnitude and reports correlations with test error, sharpness, and generalization, but does not measure weight-magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or compare it with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
